entities.summary:
Maria de Ventadorn was a prominent patron of troubadour poetry in 12th-century southern France, who played a crucial role in shaping the cultural landscape of the region.

 As a member of the nobility, de Ventadorn's influence extended beyond the artistic realm, with her connections to the Catholic Church and the royal court of France.

 Her legacy can be seen in the works of poets such as Bertran de Born and Peire Vidal, who were inspired by her patronage and went on to create some of the most iconic works of troubadour literature.

 The impact of de Ventadorn's patronage can still be felt today, with her name becoming synonymous with the golden age of troubadour poetry and her influence extending to the development of French literature and culture.

 In her own time, de Ventadorn's patronage was seen as a key factor in the flourishing of artistic and literary innovation in southern France, cementing her place as one of the most important figures of the medieval period.
